name: manual_715024
claim: expunge-all-workspace-repos.sh's multi-repo, multi-branch force-push loop cannot be swapped for publish-clean-branch.sh one-for-one -- it is a genuine architectural mismatch, not a one-line fix

decisions.notes: CodeRabbit review #4984716341 on AlphaClaw PR #29 (finding 4, Major) asked both .cursor/rules/never-undo-attribution-expunge.mdc and zero-banned-attribution-everywhere.mdc to require ALL publishing -- including scripts/git/expunge-all-workspace-repos.sh -- to route through scripts/git/publish-clean-branch.sh, with no raw force pushes. Investigated 2026-08-21: publish-clean-branch.sh is single-repo (cd's via $SCRIPT_DIR/../..) and single-branch (takes one branch arg, defaults to current), and its audit_attribution.sh range logic assumes a sensible base branch (${remote}/${base}..${branch}). expunge-all-workspace-repos.sh's force_push_repo() iterates every local branch across every repo under $WORKSPACE_ROOT after a full-history filter-branch rewrite -- main..main is an empty range, and arbitrary branches post-rewrite may have no clean ancestry against main. publish-clean-branch.sh DOES already have a HISTORY_SURGERY_PUSH=1 mode with the exact same force-with-lease + hooks-off + history-surgery-git.sh push semantics expunge uses, PLUS a stronger audit_attribution.sh + repo_hygiene.py + scan-tracked-banned-tokens.sh scan the expunge script's own before/after banned-metadata count check doesn't run. Confirmed the mismatch exists identically in orama-system's canonical copy (not just a PT/AlphaClaw drift), so the fix belongs there, not as a local hand-edit in any downstream repo.
